title: Lawsuit claims AI helps drive higher fast-food prices
source_used: WSB-TV (Cox Media Group, citing the Associated Press) and Top Class Actions, both read in full; NewsNation page blocked (403)
key_facts: A lawsuit filed in federal court in Illinois accuses McDonald's of using an AI pricing tool that collects data franchise competitors would not normally share, including store-level sales (WSB-TV, citing the Associated Press).
The complaint calls the result "algorithmic price-fixing aimed at customers who are already stretched thin" and says the system raises McDonald's US prices.
McDonald's says AI does not set menu prices, franchisees do; optional tools help franchisees but do not automate, coordinate or fix prices.
McDonald's says it has used an AI-enhanced pricing tool for more than a decade.

Top Class Actions: Michael Thomas v. McDonald's USA LLC et al., Case No. 1:26-cv-12149, US District Court, Northern District of Illinois; proposed nationwide class; claims under the Sherman Act and Illinois laws; seeks damages including treble damages.
The complaint says about 95% of McDonald's US restaurants are franchises and alleges a centralised machine-learning pricing engine since at least 2019.
Reuters has reported several suits over AI and pricing in hotels, real estate and health insurance, using antitrust law.
WSB-TV (9 Oct 2026) says the suit was filed 'last week'; our 6 Oct edition (Reuters) says filed 2 Oct 2026.
quote_evidence: The lawsuit, filed last week in federal court in Illinois, claims the pricing tool uses AI to collect data that franchise competitors would not typically share.
The fast-food giant said it does not use AI to set prices.
“AI does not set menu prices at McDonald’s restaurants – McDonald’s franchisees do,” the company said in a statement.
why_it_matters_hint: Tests whether AI-assisted pricing across franchise restaurants can amount to price-fixing; the claims are unproven.
event_date: Suit filed 2 Oct 2026 (our 6 Oct edition, Reuters); WSB-TV article dated 9 Oct 2026.
